title: Optimizing exercise training for chronic non-specific low back pain: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
summary: This study aims to find out how often people with persistent low back pain should exercise for the best results. Specifically, we are comparing a once-a-week approach to a three-times-a-week approach to see which is more effective. We will also assess whether the exercises are safe, how well people adhere to the program, and how satisfied they are with the treatment. The findings will help design a larger study in the future that aims to further identify exercise-based strategies to improve the lives of people with persistent low back pain.

interventions.name: Participants in both exercise groups will follow similar exercise components (stabilization and resistance training) with different frequency protocols. Over the course of six weeks, participants in the two training groups will engage in supervised exercise training sessions lasting 20–25 minutes. T

High-frequency exercise group (Group B)
Each participant in group B will receive a total of 18 supervised sessions with a frequency of three exercise training sessions per week. 

Participants in Groups A and B will additionally complete a once-weekly, non-supervised home-based exercise program.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
average pain intensity of at least 40 on the Visual Analog Scale
Exclusion criteria:
- Actively participating in moderate-vigorous exercises for more than 150 minutes per week
- Currently receiving or have undertaken physiotherapy or exercise treatment for low back pain in the previous month
- Unable to attend three training sessions per week and four testing sessions over the course of 12 weeks
- Specific or radicular syndrome low back pain
- Inability to communicate in English  
- Current pregnancy
- Less than one-year post-partum 
- Current clinical diagnosis of severe depression, acute anxiety disorders, schizophrenia, or other severe mental health conditions
- Stroke
- Traumatic brain injury
- Other absolute contraindications to exercise training
- Unable to provide informed consent (e.g. cognitive impairment)
